cause_quote: The PostgreSQL port added jsonPathValue as `(${value}::jsonb #>> ...)` and routed the model-context, history-input-visibility and mirror transcript readers through it, so any stored event whose JSON holds an escaped lone surrogate or NUL fails the jsonb cast.
user_saw: On a PostgreSQL-backed Gateway, every follow-up turn in a session whose transcript held a lone surrogate escape failed with 22P02, and a user message containing NUL was dropped with 22021.
summary: Routes PostgreSQL transcript and model-context reads through the jsonNativeFieldsValid (jsonb-validity) guard so rows jsonb rejects are decoded in JavaScript, and replaces NUL with a space in the derived full-text index text.
reasoning: SQLite accepts these escapes, so the failure exists only on the PostgreSQL path, which was created by #171545 (93e8fe35376) adding `::jsonb` casts in jsonPathValue and wiring the transcript readers to it; the edge case was never handled there, and #183560 later added the guard for some readers but not these. Medium rather than high because the NUL full-text index failure and a few guarded readers trace to sibling Postgres-port commits (e.g. #174786, #183560), not only #171545.
